page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores using an x86_64 architecture. The underlying processor is an Intel Xeon 6973P-C operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance. In stress-ng multi-core tests and PassMark CPU evaluations, the server ranks in the top 10% of tested systems. This high performance is supported by advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning acceleration. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also place the system in the top 10%, although the PassMark memory score falls into the middle 50%. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core results ranking in the middle 50%.

The D128s_v7 demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput both achieve top-tier performance. For AI workloads, the server delivers strong prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large language models, though text generation speeds are more moderate. Given its high resource density and dedicated compute allocation, the server offers a robust profile for enterprise-grade multi-threaded workloads, web serving, and database management, representing a high-capacity general-purpose option without the overhead of local storage.
